text: It needs just to reach a neighbor that is close by. So this allows A to save power and therefore energy, and as we already said, has got also as a good consequence, positive consequence, the fact that the interfering range will be smaller. So we are not going to interfere much with other nodes that we want to transmit. We already know that the level of power that is received at a certain point in space follows this law, where d is the distance here between a transmitter and a receiver. We said in free space, this exponent alpha is exactly equal to two. In real world environments, when we do not have propagation in free space, this exponent value is greater than than two, so the power decay is more rapidly. So we need to be, let's say, smart in controlling the transmission power of the nodes. It must be sufficiently high to reach the intended receiver, in spite of the fact that the signal may get attenuated due to distance, diffraction, reflection, etc. But it shouldn't be too high, right? Because otherwise you consume too much.
